news.title: Lionesses take control of World Cup playoff tie but unfancied Greece still in fight
news.lede: World Cup qualifying playoff: Greece 1-3 England. Stanway, Le Tissier and Russo on target. Sarina Wiegman admitted she wanted to see a bit more from her side after their fairly underwhelming performance against a hugely unfancied Greek side, despite securing a valuable first-leg victory in their Women’s World Cup playoff tie. Georgia Stanway’s neat finish, Maya Le Tissier’s first England goal and Alessia Russo’s low strike were enough to give England control but a Ioanna Papatheodorou goal for Greece means that the tie is not definitively over, going into Tuesday’s second leg, and Wiegman acknowledged that England had been “a bit sloppy” at times.

news.title: Russo’s return to form is vital but Lionesses still lack bite against low blocks | Suzanne Wrack
news.lede: England have the edge over Greece after the first leg of their World Cup playoff but remain a team in transition. It took a labyrinthine move from Sarina Wiegman’s team to find a way through deep-lying Greece. On the outskirts of Heraklion, the ancient city of Knossos, which is associated with the legend of the Minotaur and the labyrinth constructed by Daedalus to contain it, Laura Blindkilde Brown’s quick pass to Alessia Russo was artfully flicked first time to her Arsenal teammate Georgia Stanway and the midfielder slotted in past the goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti. There were muted celebrations following the goal, reflective of the frustration they felt at having taken 39 minutes to get their first goal against the team ranked 54 places below them.

news.title: England are in control of their World Cup play-off with Greece after winning the first leg 3-1 in Crete.
news.lede: Goals from Georgia Stanway, Maya Le Tissier and Alessia Russo moved the Lionesses into a strong position for Tuesday's second leg in Leicester - although Calliste Brookshire, who plays for Rangers in Scotland, pulled one back late on for a Greece side ranked 58th in the world. The winner will play Slovakia or Ukraine in round two on the road to Brazil 2027. Lauren James saw a stunning chip from long range ruled out for offside in the first half but the Lionesses - forced into the play-offs after finishing behind Spain in qualifying - were not at their sharpest in that period and they were almost shocked when Ioanna Papatheodorou cracked a shot against the crossbar from 35 yards. news.title: Wales must improve after Women's World Cup play-off win in Albania - Rhian Wilkinson
news.lede: Rhian Wilkinson is hoping to lead Wales to a first Women's World Cup. Rhian Wilkinson accepted Wales must raise their standards after they scraped to a 1-0 victory in their Women's World Cup play-off semi-final in Albania. Wales have the upper hand going into Tuesday's second leg in Llanelli after Ezmiralda Franja's first-half own goal gave them victory in Shkoder. But Wilkinson's team were fortunate to triumph against a team who sit 37 places below them in the Fifa rankings after Albania created the game's best chances.

news.title: Wexford School to represent Ireland at School World Cup in China
news.lede: The senior team at Wexford CBS are set to travel to Suzhou, China to represent Ireland at the 2026 International School Sport Federation Football World Cup. The team was invited to take part after they won the FAI Under-17 National Junior Cup in 2025. They will become the first Irish team to compete in the tournament since St Benildus College headed to Sardinia in 1999. They will leave for Shanghai on 14 October, before travelling to Suzhou for the start of the tournament on 18 October.

news.title: Morocco U-17 Women’s Team Coach Reveals World Cup Squad
news.lede: Rabat - Morocco U-17 women’s national team coach Younes Rabie has revealed the final list of players called up to represent the country at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. The tournament will be hosted by Morocco from October 17 to November 8, giving the young Atlas Lionesses the opportunity to compete on home soil in a major international tournament. The squad list: Fatiha Naam Meriem Zeqaqi Chaymae Bouzrou Laila Boushaba Malak Krafia Anissa Hamdani Hiba Youssoufi Imene Diyen Charaf Boughazi Meryam Oubella Rita El Miroun Nayla Aagaou Sofia Ben Amar Sara El Hajjiouti Nora El Rhachoua Wachol Sonia Abajiou Nessma Mouradi Aya Ait Khouya Imane Dhissi Amana Lakradi The squad will now enter the final stage of preparations ahead of the competition, with the coaching staff using two closed-door friendly matches to assess the team and fine-tune its preparations.
